column1: # Candidate lineage names for every APSE genome in the panel.
# Lineages were defined by single-linkage clustering on 31-mer containment at a
# 0.95 threshold. The data separate cleanly: within a group containment is
# 0.98-1.00, between groups 0.55-0.75, with almost nothing in between.
# Naming is APSE-<toxin>-<numeral>. The toxin is kept because it is the useful
# biological label; the numeral is what prevents the name implying that two
# phages sharing a toxin are the same lineage. They frequently are not: this
# panel contains three distinct CdtB lineages and two distinct RHS lineages,
# and the published APSE-1 carries the same Shiga-like toxin as S09 while
# sharing only 62 % of its 31-mers with it.
# CORRECTION 2026-08-03: S08 and S10 were initially grouped together as MAC-I.
# That was an artefact of S10's sequence being partial. With S10 rebuilt to
# 34,095 bp, containment between S08 and S10 is only 0.550 -- they are DIFFERENT
# lineages. S14's 19,800 bp fragment lies in sequence the two share (0.979 to
# S08, 0.998 to S10) and cannot be assigned to either. A partial genome cannot
# be assigned to a lineage when the candidates share a backbone.
# Integrase type is recorded but deliberately NOT part of the name: 16 of the 18
# genomes examined carry type A (99.1-100 % identity), and only the CdtB-II
# lineage carries type B. A character that is invariant across nine tenths of the
# panel adds nothing to a name, and putting it there would imply it defines
# lineages when it does not. It matters for a different reason -- it determines
# the att core and therefore which chromosomal site the phage occupies.
# status: confirmed  = complete genome, unambiguous group membership
#         partial    = only part of the phage recovered; grouping is supported
#                      but rests on less sequence
#         unresolved = too little sequence recovered to assign
